jobs.title: Channels and Partnerships Lead
jobs.description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

We're hiring our first Partnerships Lead to build the partner ecosystem that will become a force multiplier for Artemis's growth.

Parters are not our distribution strategy-they are a growth strategy. They influence buying decisions, accelerate trust, drive deployments, and expand market reach. The right ecosystem can create outsized leverage for an early-stage company.

This is a builder role.

You'll define Artemis's partner ecosystem strategy from the ground up, recruit and activate strategic partners, establish repeatable partner motions, and build the operational foundation for a world-class channel and alliances organization.

You'll work directly with the founders and partner closely with Sales, Product, Marketing, Customer Success, and Engineering.

Success in this role means turning partnerships into measurable revenue, market awareness, customer outcomes, and strategic advantage.




RESPONSIBILITIES




BUILD THE ECOSYSTEM STRATEGY

 - Develop and execute Artemis's partner strategy across:
   
   - Strategic channels and technology alliances
   
   - Cloud providers
   
   - Security platforms
   
   - MSSPs and MDRs
   
   - Value-added resellers
   
   - Global Systems Integrators (Accenture, Deloitte, EY)
   
   - Regional and boutique consulting partners


RECRUIT AND ACTIVATE STRATEGIC PARTNERS

 - Identify, recruit, and activate the first wave of strategic partners aligned with Artemis's target customer profile.

 - Prioritize partner investments based on revenue potential, market influence, technical alignment, and customer reach.

 - Establish executive relationships across partner organizations.


BUILD REPEATABLE PARTNER OPERATIONS

 - Create and operationalize:
   
   - Partner program framework
   
   - Deal registration
   
   - Rules of engagement
   
   - Incentive structures
   
   - Partner Marketing strategy
   
   - Referral and reseller motions
   
   - Marketplace strategy
   
   - Partner success metrics and operational best practices


EXECUTE JOINT GO-TO-MARKET

 - Build partner business plans and quarterly success metrics.

 - Develop joint sales plays, campaigns, events, workshops, and executive engagement programs.

 - Drive co-sell motions and marketplace opportunities.

 - Coordinate pipeline generation activities with Sales and Marketing.


BUILD WORLD-CLASS ENABLEMENT

 - Build partner enablement strategy and partner cross-functionallly to deliver assets, training, demo environments, battlecards, technical documentation-that let partners use, sell and deploy Artemis (products and services) with confidence


OWN REVENUE OUTCOMES

 - Drive partner-sourced and partner-influenced pipeline.

 - Establish partner contribution as a measurable component of company growth.

 - Build forecasting and reporting mechanisms for partner performance.
   
   


QUALIFICATIONS

 - 7+ years of experience in partnerships, alliances, channel sales, ecosystem development, or business development.

 - 3+ years within cybersecurity, cloud, or enterprise infrastructure.

 - Demonstrated success building partner programs from an early-stage or growth-stage environment.

 - Proven ability to generate measurable pipeline and revenue through partnerships.

 - Strong trusted network of channel and tech alliance partners

 - Experience building executive-level relationships and influencing senior stakeholders.

 - Strong operational discipline with the ability to build scalable processes from scratch.

 - Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills.

 - Comfortable operating in ambiguity and moving quickly with limited resources.





NICE TO HAVE

 - Prior experience as the first partnerships or channel hire at a cybersecurity startup.

 - Experience helping scale a company from Series A through growth stage.

 - Background in sales engineering, product management, consulting, or enterprise sales.

 - Experience with cloud marketplaces and co-sell programs.

 - Existing relationships with AWS, CrowdStrike, Google, Accenture, Deloitte, EY, Optiv, GuidePoint, WWT, and major MSSPs.

 - Experience structuring OEM, embedded technology, and strategic ecosystem partnerships.

 - Familiarity with AI-native security, security operations, threat intelligence, and enterprise security architectures.

jobs.title: Technology Alliances Manager
jobs.description:
About Artemis

Artemis is building the future of AI-driven defense - helping companies detect and defend themselves effectively in an era where AI is fighting AI on the cyber battlefield. We're in hypergrowth and already protect customers like Cursor, Lemonade, and Wix as well as some of the biggest enterprises in the world.

About the Role

Most companies treat technology alliances as a nice-to-have. At Artemis, alliances are closer to how the product works. Our platform runs on AWS and reasons over telemetry that lives in other vendors' systems: EDR, SIEM, identity, cloud, and the pipelines that move security data between them. Every one of those vendors is simultaneously an integration, a channel, and a reason a customer picks us. The companies we plug into are the companies we go to market with.

We're hiring a Technology Alliances Manager to own that motion end to end, with three tracks front and center:

 - Hyperscalers. AWS first: we build on it and our customers run on it. Own the relationship end to end: Marketplace transactability and private offers, co-sell through ISV Accelerate, competency milestones, and the AWS field teams who can put us in front of their accounts.

 - Security platforms. The largest vendors in security (CrowdStrike, Palo Alto Networks, and their peers) already collect the telemetry we investigate. Build the alliances that position Artemis as a multiplier on their platforms: partnership agreements, store listings, certified integrations, and field-level co-sell.

 - ISVs. The vendors that shape and route security data (Cribl and its peers) as well as domain specific security companies helps us secure customers together. Build the reference architectures and joint plays that helps customers stay safe.

Many of these relationships are already in motion at the executive level. Your job is to take them from conversations to signed, integrated, revenue-producing partnerships, and to decide what we pursue next.

We're not collecting logos. A partnership counts when it produces something measurable: sourced pipeline, marketplace revenue, an integration customers actually turn on, a partner seller who pulls us into a deal. You'll be measured on those outcomes, and you'll have the product, engineering, and executive support to hit them.

Responsibilities

 - Own the technology partner map: which partners, in what order, for what outcome; double down on what performs and kill what doesn't

 - Run the AWS motion end to end: Marketplace listing and private offers, co-sell pipeline, program and competency milestones, and joint content with AWS field and specialist teams

 - Build and negotiate alliances with the major security platforms: agreements, integration roadmaps, marketplace listings, and better-together assets (solution briefs, reference architectures, joint demos) that sales actually uses

 - Drive integrations from scoping to launch with product and engineering on both sides, and make sure every launch ships with a go-to-market moment, not just a docs page

 - Turn partnerships into revenue: joint account mapping, co-sell registrations, warm intros, MDF, and partner events (RSA, re:Invent, Fal.Con, Black Hat), with tracking of alliance-sourced and alliance-influenced pipeline

 - Bring partner and market signal back into product roadmap and positioning

What Success Looks Like in Year One

 - Artemis transacts on AWS Marketplace with an active co-sell motion and registered opportunities flowing in both directions

 - Two or three anchor alliances with major security vendors are signed, integrated, and producing referred deals

 - Every anchor partner has a better-together kit our sales team actually pulls up in live deals

 - Alliance-sourced and alliance-influenced pipeline is a tracked, growing number the whole company can see

Move at rocket speed, build something massive.

Artemis is an early-stage cybersecurity company solving problems that matter, against adversaries that don't slow down. As our founding Technology Alliances Manager, you'll shape how Artemis plugs into the rest of the security stack and how customers experience us alongside every other tool they run. You'll have full ownership, real autonomy, and a direct line to leadership. The pace is fast, the bar is high, and the impact is direct.

Qualifications

 - 5+ years in technology alliances, partnerships, or business development at a cybersecurity or enterprise infrastructure company

 - At least one partnership you built from zero and can walk us through in numbers: what it sourced, influenced, or unlocked

 - Hands-on hyperscaler experience: you've listed and transacted on a cloud marketplace, worked programs like AWS ISV Accelerate, and know how co-sell and partner funding actually operate

 - Fluency in the security ecosystem: the major platforms across EDR/XDR, SIEM, identity, and data pipeline, how they interoperate, and what their partner organizations optimize for

 - Range: technical enough to whiteboard an integration with partner engineers, commercial enough to negotiate the agreement behind it, credible with partner executives

 - Judgment for coopetition: some of our most important partners also ship competing products, and you know how to build the better-together lane anyway

 - Comfort with ambiguity, building from scratch, and moving fast without dropping details

Nice to Have

 - Time inside the partner organization of a hyperscaler or major security platform: you know how AWS, CrowdStrike, or Palo Alto Networks evaluate ISV partners from the inside

 - Existing relationships across the security partner ecosystem

 - Experience as a company's first alliances hire

 - Familiarity with partner ecosystem tooling (Crossbeam, Tackle, WorkSpan, and similar)

jobs.title: Channel Sales Manager
jobs.description:
About Artemis

Artemis is building the future of AI-driven defense – helping companies detect and defend themselves effectively in an era where AI is fighting AI on the cyber battlefield.

We’re backed by First Round Capital, Brightmind, and a group of the cybersecurity industry’s most prominent Operators.

Our founders, Shachar (ex-Palo Alto Networks, AWS, Demisto) and Dan (ex-Abnormal Security, Twitter) have previously built, launched, and scaled cybersecurity products loved and trusted by tens of thousands of customers, and have the customer, technology, and security know-hows to deliver this vision.

Our exceptionally strong team includes software engineers, AI researchers, security engineers, and product designers hailing from Google, Abnormal AI, Wiz, Meta, AWS, CERN, SentinelOne, and more.

We are growing our team and looking for passionate builders to join us and support our expanding customer base.

The Role

As our first EMEA Channel Sales Manager, you'll own building Artemis's indirect go-to-market motion in the UK and Europe. You'll identify, recruit, and enable strategic partners (Distributors Value Added Resellers, MSSP’s and GSI’s) to sell Artemis into new and existing customer base. You'll develop partner programs, provide enablement and support, manage partner relationships, and ensure partners are generating pipeline and closing deals.

This role is critical to scaling beyond direct sales. You'll have autonomy to shape our channel strategy, build partner relationships from scratch, and drive significant revenue through indirect channels.

Key Responsibilities

 - Identify and recruit strategic channel partners (Distributors, Value Added Resellers, MSSP’s and GSI’s) across the UK and Europe

 - Develop and manage partnership agreements, pricing structures, and incentive programs

 - Onboard new partners and provide initial enablement (product training, positioning, sales tools, technical certification)

 - Build partner success playbooks—what works, what messaging lands, how to close deals

 - Conduct regular business reviews with partners to monitor pipeline, revenue, and performance

 - Support partner sales teams on complex deals (technical questions, customer introductions, deal strategy)

 - Co-market with partners (joint webinars, events, case studies, campaigns)

 - Manage partner portal, training materials, and go-to-market resources

 - Build forecasting models around partner revenue and pipeline

 - Identify gaps in partner coverage and recruit to fill them

 - Collaborate with Sales, Product, and Customer Success to ensure smooth handoffs and partner success

 - Hit revenue targets tied to partner-sourced deals and pipeline

What We're Looking For

 - 5+ years in channel sales, partner sales, or indirect go-to-market roles in B2B technology or cybersecurity

 - Proven track record building channel programs from scratch or scaling existing programs

 - Strong understanding of partner types (Distributors, Value Added Resellers, MSSP’s and GSI’s) and how to recruit, enable, and manage them

 - Experience managing multiple partners simultaneously and hitting revenue targets

 - Deep network in the UK/European cybersecurity or enterprise technology space (or ability to build one quickly)

 - Comfortable negotiating partnerships, pricing, and incentive structures

 - Strong presentation and communication skills—you'll train partners and present to leadership

 - Project management skills—you'll own multiple workstreams and timelines

 - CRM and sales ops experience (Salesforce, Pipedrive, or similar)

 - Ability to balance structure with flexibility—partners need support, but you can't hand-hold forever

 - Comfortable with ambiguity and building processes from scratch

Nice to Have

 - Prior channel/partner experience (you've seen how they buy and what they want)

 - Cybersecurity or security product expertise

 - Experience building MDF (Marketing Development Funds) or partner incentive programs

 - Regional presence and relationships in UK/Europe

 - Experience at early-stage SaaS companies scaling go-to-market
